authoringProvenance.author: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Pro — unreviewed candidate generation

items.prompt: For the longest window satisfying an at-most constraint, where should `best = max(best, right - left + 1)` run?
constraints: The right value has already been added.
A while loop removes left values while the window is invalid.
Removing more values from the left cannot make a valid window invalid.

options.text: After the repair loop, when the current window is valid.
Immediately after expansion, before checking validity.
Only inside each shrink iteration.
Only once after all right-boundary steps finish.

feedback.reason: The longest answer must consume a legal state, and after repair the window is the longest valid suffix ending at the current right boundary.

blocks.text: Expansion defines all candidates ending at right, but an invalid expanded range cannot be scored. The repair loop discards exactly the starts that still violate the constraint. When it ends, [left..right] is valid and any earlier start was invalid, so this is the longest valid suffix for that right endpoint. Updating only during shrink misses right steps that need no repair; updating only at the end ignores earlier endpoints. The same placement applies to at-most budgets and frequency limits.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.before_repair: The length may describe a constraint-violating range and can inflate the result with an illegal candidate.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.inside_each_shrink: Intermediate states can remain invalid, and no update occurs on expansions that stay valid without shrinking.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.after_full_scan: The final window is not guaranteed to be the longest one encountered across all right endpoints.

items.prompt: For the shortest nonempty positive-value window with sum at least a positive target T, when should the current length update `best` during shrinking?
constraints: The current window is valid when the inner loop begins.
T is positive and only nonempty ranges are candidates.
Removing the left value may make it invalid.

options.text: Only after a removal makes the sum fall below T.
Before each left removal while the current window still satisfies sum ≥ T.
Only for the first valid window ending at each right boundary.
Only after the outer scan finishes.

feedback.reason: Each valid state is a legal candidate; it must be recorded before the next removal can destroy validity.

blocks.text: For a fixed right endpoint, the valid-loop visits successively shorter windows. The current candidate exists before its outgoing value is removed, so compare its length with best first. If a removal makes the sum invalid, that post-removal range cannot be scored, and the last valid range would be lost if updates waited until then. Recording only the first valid range misses shorter valid suffixes. This answer timing is the mirror image of longest-valid repair-first timing.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.after_invalid: The post-removal range fails the threshold, while the immediately preceding valid candidate is no longer represented.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.once_first_valid: The first valid window for a right endpoint is generally the longest; further valid removals can improve the minimum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_end: The final state may be invalid and does not summarize minimum candidates from earlier endpoints.

items.prompt: A fixed-size window requires exactly k elements. Which condition must be true before its aggregate may update the answer?
constraints: k is a positive integer.
The implementation may temporarily hold fewer than k elements during initialization and k+1 immediately after expansion.
Only exact-size candidates are legal.

options.text: Any range of length at most k may update the answer.
The aggregate is positive, regardless of length.
The maintained state and boundaries represent exactly k elements.
The right boundary moved at least once.

feedback.reason: Fixed-size answer legality is determined by exact boundary distance, not by aggregate value or traversal progress.

blocks.text: Before the first k values, the state is incomplete. Immediately after adding a new value to an established window, the range can temporarily have k+1 elements until the outgoing value is removed. Neither state matches the answer contract. Updating only at length k prevents partial and oversized ranges from competing with legal candidates. Negative aggregates remain legal, and a right move alone says nothing about size. The equality check also prevents a stale aggregate from being scored if boundary movement and state removal have not completed together.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.length_at_most_k: This silently changes an exactly-k problem into an at-most-k problem and admits shorter ranges.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sum_positive: Sign is irrelevant to whether a range contains the required number of elements.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.right_moved: Traversal progress does not guarantee that initialization or removal has produced size k.

items.prompt: A shortest-threshold scan may find no valid window. Which initialization and final check preserve that boundary correctly?
constraints: The required output distinguishes ‘no qualifying range’ from a real length.
A zero-length range is not a legal candidate.

options.text: Initialize best to 0 because 0 is the shortest possible length.
Initialize best to n and always return it, even if no range is valid.
Initialize best to −1 and minimize directly against every observed length.
Initialize best to an unreachable sentinel such as +∞; update only from valid windows; after the scan, translate an unchanged sentinel to the specified no-result value.

feedback.reason: The accumulator must start worse than every legal positive length without impersonating an actual candidate.

blocks.text: A minimum accumulator initialized to 0 can never be improved by positive window lengths and falsely suggests that an empty range qualified. Initializing to n is safe only if a valid length-n range is guaranteed or a separate found flag is maintained; otherwise n is ambiguous. A sentinel such as +∞ represents ‘not found yet’, accepts every real valid length, and is translated only after the scan according to the public output contract. This pattern also applies to best start/end indices by using an explicit optional result.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.zero_best: Zero is smaller than every legal nonempty length, so the minimum never changes and reports a fabricated empty solution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_best_always: If no range qualifies, n is returned as though the whole input were valid; a found check would still be required.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.negative_one_during_scan: Direct minimization against −1 prevents any positive length from replacing it unless special-case logic is added.

items.prompt: A longest-valid window expands with a new value and remains valid, so the shrink loop executes zero times. What should happen to the answer?
constraints: The objective is maximum valid length.
The post-expansion range is legal.

options.text: Update the answer from the expanded valid range even though left did not move.
Skip the update because answer changes belong only to shrink iterations.
Move left once so that an answer update has a shrink event.
Wait until a later expansion becomes invalid, then evaluate this earlier length.

feedback.reason: The answer is tied to a legal candidate at the current right boundary, not to whether repair work occurred.

blocks.text: When no shrink is needed, the expanded window is already the longest valid suffix ending at right and may be longer than every prior candidate. The repair loop's role is only to restore validity when necessary. Conditioning the update on loop execution loses exactly the easy valid expansions that often build the optimum. Forcing a shrink discards legal length, and deferring cannot reconstruct every earlier boundary state reliably. Place the update after the loop so it executes for both zero and many repairs.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.skip_without_shrink: A valid expansion can create a new maximum; no repair event is required for candidate legitimacy.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.force_one_shrink: This deliberately shortens a valid candidate and can destroy the optimum.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.defer_until_invalid: Later state does not preserve the exact earlier window, and the answer should be updated when the candidate is known legal.

items.prompt: After repairing an at-most-K window for a fixed right boundary, every start index from left through right forms a valid suffix. How should a count-all answer use this state?
constraints: The goal is to count all valid contiguous ranges, not find a longest one.
K is a nonnegative integer.
Validity is hereditary under removing more elements from the left.

options.text: Update only the maximum length and add one range for this right boundary.
Add right − left + 1 because that is the number of valid suffixes ending at right.
Add left because it counts how many values were removed.
Count only [left..right]; shorter suffixes require separate scans.

feedback.reason: A repaired hereditary at-most window compactly represents one valid suffix for every start in [left..right].

blocks.text: There are right−left+1 possible starts in the current window. Removing additional leading elements cannot violate an at-most constraint, so each suffix [s..right] for s from left to right is valid. Adding the window length counts all of them in O(1) for this endpoint. A max update answers a different question, and counting only the widest suffix undercounts. This transfer is valid only when validity is hereditary under left removal; exact-K or at-least constraints need a different counting derivation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.take_max_length: Maximum length discards the number of shorter valid suffixes and solves an optimization rather than a count-all contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.add_left: left measures the excluded prefix, not the number of valid starts inside the current range.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.count_only_exact_window: Every shorter suffix is already known valid under an at-most predicate, so counting only one loses information represented by the boundary.

items.prompt: A variable window seeks the longest valid range. When right expands and the predicate becomes invalid, when should the candidate answer be updated?

options.text: After removing from the left until the window satisfies the predicate again; only then is its length a legal candidate.
Before shrinking, because the invalid range is temporarily the longest.
Only the final window matters, so intermediate legal states can be ignored.
Before adding right, because every previous answer already covers the new candidate.

feedback.reason: Only legal windows may compete for a longest-valid answer.

blocks.text: An invalid expanded range is not an admissible answer, even if it is longer than prior legal ranges. Shrink until the invariant holds, then compare the repaired length with the best answer. Updating before repair stores a candidate that violates the problem constraint.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.before_repair: The expanded range is invalid, so its length cannot be recorded as a legal answer.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.never_update: A maximum may occur at an intermediate repaired state before later expansions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.before_expand: The new right element can create a new legal maximum after repair.

constraints: The answer itself must satisfy the window predicate.

items.prompt: A shortest-valid-window routine returns the minimum length among legal windows. What result should it return when no legal window is ever found?

options.text: An explicit unavailable sentinel such as 0 or -1 according to the API contract, rather than a plausible positive length.
Zero always means a valid empty window, regardless of the problem's nonempty-window requirement.
n, because the entire input is the fallback candidate.
Positive infinity, even if the public return type is an integer length.

feedback.reason: An optimization over an empty feasible set needs an explicit absence representation compatible with the API.

blocks.text: Initialize the best length to an internal value that cannot be confused with a legal answer, then translate it to the documented unavailable result when no update occurred. Whether that result is 0, -1, or an option type depends on the contract and whether empty windows are legal.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.zero_always: Zero is valid only if the contract explicitly allows an empty window or defines zero as absence.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n: The entire input may be invalid and cannot be invented as a fallback.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.infinity_public: The sentinel must be representable by the public return type or converted before returning.

constraints: The API distinguishes no solution from a positive valid length.

items.prompt: A fixed-size window must emit every complete window's score, including scores smaller than the best seen so far. Which update rule is correct?

options.text: Once the window has exactly k elements, emit or record its score on every right step after removing the leaving element.
Emit only when the current score improves the global best.
Emit partial windows before they reach size k so no endpoint is skipped.
Use a variable-window shrink loop even though every legal candidate has fixed size k.

feedback.reason: The output contract contains every complete fixed-size window, not only an optimization over their scores.

blocks.text: After the first k values, each next value creates one new complete window: add the entering contribution, remove the leaving contribution, then emit. A global maximum is a different contract, and partial prefixes are not legal exact-size windows.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.emit_only_best: The contract requires all complete windows, including non-best scores.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.emit_before_fill: Partial prefixes do not satisfy the exact-size constraint.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.shrink_until_valid: Fixed size determines left movement; there is no variable validity repair here.

constraints: Every output corresponds to exactly k consecutive elements.

items.prompt: For an at-most-K distinct window, after repair at right, why can the answer count add right - left + 1 even if the current window is not the longest seen?

options.text: Every suffix starting at s in [left, right] remains at-most-K distinct, so the state represents that many valid ranges ending at right.
The current window is always the global longest, so the formula is a disguised maximum update.
Only [left, right] is valid; shorter suffixes can introduce more distinct values.
left counts valid ranges because it is the number of shrink operations.

feedback.reason: At-most validity is hereditary under removing a prefix, so one repaired boundary counts all valid suffixes for that right endpoint.

blocks.text: Once [left, right] has at most K distinct values, removing elements from its left cannot create a new distinct value. Every start from left through right therefore yields a valid range ending at right, and their count is the window length. This is a counting identity, not a longest-window update.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.only_longest: Counting valid suffixes is independent of which window is globally longest.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.invalid_suffixes: Removing a prefix cannot increase distinct count under an at-most predicate.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.add_left: The number of valid starts is right-left+1, not left.

constraints: Validity is at-most-K distinct and hereditary under left removal.

items.prompt: For a longest-valid-window problem, when should the candidate length update the best answer?
constraints: The current window must satisfy the validity predicate.
The left boundary may move during repair.

options.text: After shrinking has restored validity, record the current valid window length.
options.explanation: A temporarily invalid window is not an eligible answer.

options.text: Record the expanded length before removing invalid elements.
options.explanation: The recorded window may violate the contract.

options.text: Record every left-pointer position even if the window remains invalid.
options.explanation: Answer states must satisfy the predicate.

options.text: Record only the final window after the entire scan ends.

feedback.reason: The answer update must observe the same legal state that the problem asks to optimize.

blocks.text: Expansion can temporarily violate the constraint, but the repaired window is the candidate. Updating only then keeps the answer invariant valid and preserves earlier optima through max/min aggregation.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.before_repair: The recorded window may violate the contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.every_left_move: Answer states must satisfy the predicate.

items.prompt: For a shortest-valid-window objective, what must be done while a current window satisfies the predicate?
constraints: Removing the leftmost item may eventually break validity.
The objective is minimum length.

options.text: Record its length, then shrink from the left while validity remains true to search for the shortest valid suffix.
options.explanation: Every valid left boundary is a candidate for the minimum.

options.text: Keep expanding because a larger valid window contains more evidence.
options.explanation: Larger windows are worse for a minimum-length objective.

options.text: Remove until invalid, then record the invalid length as the boundary optimum.
Reset both pointers after the first valid window so no later state can overlap it.
options.explanation: Overlapping candidate windows are essential to finding the minimum.

feedback.reason: Minimum objectives need a legal-state update before each shrink that remains legal.

blocks.text: Once valid, every left boundary before the first invalid removal is a candidate. The algorithm records each and stops shrinking only when the predicate would fail, then expands again.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.expand_only: Larger windows are worse for a minimum-length objective.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reset_window: Overlapping candidate windows are essential to finding the minimum.

items.prompt: How many windows of length k should a fixed-size scan emit for an input of length n when 1<=k<=n?
constraints: Every contiguous window must be reported exactly once.
The window advances one position at a time.

options.text: Emit n−k+1 windows, one for each possible start index from 0 through n−k.
options.explanation: Those are exactly the valid fixed-length starts.

options.text: Emit n+k windows because each expansion and shrink creates a result.
options.explanation: Internal pointer operations are not distinct windows.

options.text: Emit floor(n/k) windows because windows must be disjoint.
options.explanation: A sliding window enumerates overlapping windows.

options.text: Emit n windows regardless of k.
options.explanation: The number of starts depends on the requested length.

feedback.reason: The fixed-size output contract is determined by the set of legal start positions.

blocks.text: Overlapping windows are distinct outputs. There are n−k+1 starts, and a correct scan updates the outgoing and incoming state once per shift.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_plus_k: Internal pointer operations are not distinct windows.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_div_k: A sliding window enumerates overlapping windows.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.n_only: The number of starts depends on the requested length.

items.prompt: What should a fixed-size window routine do when k is greater than the input length?
constraints: No contiguous window of length k exists.
The API defines an explicit unavailable-result policy.

options.text: Return the contract's empty or unavailable result without pretending that a shorter window is valid.
options.explanation: The requested window length is not present.

options.text: Use the whole input as a substitute window of length n.
Pad the input with zeros so one window can be emitted.
options.explanation: Padding invents data not in the input contract.

options.text: Return n−k+1 as a negative number of windows.
options.explanation: A count of outputs cannot be negative; the boundary needs an explicit policy.

feedback.reason: The no-window case is an output contract, not a reason to silently change k.

blocks.text: A fixed-size routine should expose absence explicitly—often an empty collection or an unavailable answer. Substitution or padding hides the mismatch between requested and available data.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.pad_values: Padding invents data not in the input contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.emit_negative: A count of outputs cannot be negative; the boundary needs an explicit policy.
